container: The digital divide describes the gap between people who can access reliable technology and those who cannot. This gap affects education, work, health, and participation in society. Rural communities may lack strong networks, while low income households often must share devices or rely on costly mobile data. Older adults and people unfamiliar with technology may need patient guidance. Closing the divide requires investment in internet infrastructure, affordable devices, and public access points such as libraries. Schools can teach digital literacy, and communities can offer support in multiple languages. Governments and technology companies should work together to make services accessible and protect users online. Better access helps people learn, connect, find work, and take part in civic life. Technology should expand opportunity for everyone.
